subject: peter-ralston

article.title: Draft:Peter Ralston
article.coi: The requester (Wikipedia user Biofuel) authored the previous article on this subject, deleted at AfD in 2010 and again 2026-09-15 (2nd nomination, closed by Vanamonde93), and knows practitioners in the subject's milieu. AfC review required — mainspace recreation is G4-eligible.
article.note: A live Draft:Peter Ralston page now exists (revid 1376596028) — substantially this project's draft, posted and lightly edited. Items are assessed against that revision.

gng.note: Internal assessment — 5 independent sources cover the 1978 championship: Oakland Tribune Apr 1978 + Black Belt Dec 1978 (both contemporaneous), SF Chronicle Sep 1979, Parade Mar 1982, Blitz Aug 2011. Submission wording asks reviewers to assess; the draft does not claim it.

items.claim: In 1978 Ralston won the light-heavyweight title at the Second World Kuoshu Martial Arts Tournament near Taipei, Taiwan.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous — reported Apr 12, 1978, weeks after the event; names event + division
Black Belt Dec 1978 pp.46–49 feature — verified inside the Google Books scan (id w9QDAAAAMBAJ)
Bills him 'World martial arts champion' in a Bay-Area feature
Syndicated ~60 papers on 1982-03-07; ~200-word item with original interview
Blitz Aug 2011 pp.70–74 retrospective via doczz scan + Wayback captures of blitzmag.net

items.rationale: Core notability claim — two contemporaneous + three retrospective independent sources. Organizer/governing body still unidentified (open task).

rationale_blocks.title: AfD point-by-point (why this draft is different)
rationale_blocks.body:
| AfD objection (2nd nom) | Response |
|---|---|
| 'everything covering him is trivial or self-pub' | Five independent sources now cited, two contemporaneous: Oakland Tribune 1978-04-12 p.25, Black Belt Dec 1978 pp.46–49, SF Chronicle 1979-09-19 p.4, Parade 1982-03-07 p.18, Blitz Aug 2011 pp.70–74 |
| 'no supporting evidence for world championship' | Tribune names the actual event ('Second World Kuoshu Martial Arts Tournament', light-heavyweight) within weeks; Black Belt covered it same year |
| 'hasn't gained notability since last deletion' | Argument rests on print-era coverage 1978–2011, not web bios |
| disambiguation — same-named photographer | Draft targets 'Peter Ralston (martial artist)' per the nom's own suggestion |

rationale_blocks.title: Source verification notes
rationale_blocks.body: Black Belt: verified inside the Google Books scan of the Dec 1978 issue (article begins p.46; byline OCRs 'Cressey', secondary refs 'Cressy' — flagged). Parade: clipbook scan corroborated by ~60 newspapers carrying the identical Significa page 1982-03-07 (Peoria Journal Star OCR verbatim; Mississippi Press teased it Mar 4). Blitz: publisher's own reproduction archived at web.archive.org (blitzmag.net, captures 2014–16); issue identity via MA-Mags index (Vol 25 No 8 = Aug 2011); doczz.net hosts the issue scan.

rationale_blocks.title: Sourcing checklist status (detail)
rationale_blocks.body: A. Black Belt Dec 1978: issue obtained (Google Books w9QDAAAAMBAJ), title 'Cheng Hsin: Essence of All Martial Arts', Vol 16 No 12 pp.46–49, Ralston principal subject, calls the event 'Second World Championship Chinese Martial Arts (kuoshu) Tournament'. OPEN: byline spelling on page image; full paragraph map; GNG sufficiency left to reviewers. B. Blitz Aug 2011: Vol 25 No 8 pp.70–74, title 'The Man Behind Bloodsport?' (question mark per publisher repro), interviewer Mark Grzic, ~4–5 pages direct coverage. OPEN: edited-vs-promotional read; reliance on Ralston's own account for the 1978 result. C. Parade 1982-03-07: 'Yankee Judo Dandy' (Wallace/Wallechinsky/Wallace) p.18, ~200-word item with original interview — substantial mention not full profile; IA clipbook p.19 (printed p.18) verified verbatim against newspaper prints. D. Additional profiles: EWJ Nov 1979 unlocated; 'Karate Illustrated 1981' unverified lead; newspaper DBs searched 1975–1990 (129-hit corpus triaged — found Tribune + Chronicle); WorldCat/academic passes open. E. Independence audit: chenghsin.com/Penguin author-bio/usadojo excluded from GNG count; derivative bios (wikitia, en-academic, readershouse, novelistpost) excluded. F. World-championship claim: official name recorded verbatim from both variants; Taipei area early 1978 verified; light-heavyweight confirmed; organizer + ruleset open; 'first American'/'first non-Asian' framings kept separate and attributed. G. Submission: inline citations on contested claims, page numbers for print, neutral wording, GNG not claimed, AfC path due to COI, COI disclosure kept on draft talk.
